MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  AUGUST 26, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne  Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:31 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Government
  Code section 54956.9
  Number of potential cases: (l)

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 6:34 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne  Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director;
  Maureen'Tamuri, Interim Planning Director; Susan Duenas, Public Safety Director; Rob
   DuBoux, Public Works Diractor; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Mahan Amirkian,
  Information Systems Analyst; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk; Tyler Eaton, Senior
  Planning; and Joseph Smith, Contract Planner

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Don Schmitz led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attomey Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54957, with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council discussed the items on the
  Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  August l6, 2024.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda, hearing Item Nos. 6.A. and 7.A. before Item No. 4.A. The
  motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation of City Tile to Mahan Amirkian for Seven Years of Service to the City
  of Malibu

  Mayor Stewart presented the City Tile to Mahan Amirkian.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Andrew Weyman deferred time to Terry Davis.

  Terry Davis, Big Rock Mesa Property Owner’s Association, read a letter regarding
  code enforcement and large unpermitted parties. She discussed a recent party in
  Big Rock and her report to Code Enforcement. She discussed the Council’s
  direction for ZORACES to review the City’s code enforcement fines and penalties.

  Patrick Murphree deferred time to Joe Sichta.

  Joe Sichta, Malibu Aquatics Foundation (MAF), stated MAF members addressed
  the Parks and Recreation Commission at its last meeting and discussed flaws in the
  selection process of the swim program Request for Qualifications (RFQ). He
 requested a review of the process. He discussed the minutes of the June 24, 2024
Regular meeting and stated Councilmember Silverstein and Mayor Stewart had
both requested the City Council vote on the swim contract. He discussed the limited
p001 hours for athletic programs and the number of individuals signed up for water
polo. He discussed potential opportunities to allocate pool hours for MAF.

Ludwig Brinkman deferred time to Robert Brinkman.

Olea Brinkman deferred time to Robert Brinkman.

Robert Brinkman stated the Malibu Marlins had been awarded the swim contract
and he did not see a need to revisit the award. He read a letter regarding the
formation of the Malibu Marlins and conflict with MAF. He discussed USA
Swimming and its guidelines for swim programs.

Marissa Coughlan recommended the Council adopt a Code of Conduct and amend
the Malibu Municipal Code to allow the Council to remove a Commissioner from
their position.

Hashi Clark deferred time to Kraig Hill.

Kraig Hill apologized for his behavior at the last Planning Commission meeting.
He discussed issues with the Housing Element and the public hearing for the
Housing Element. He discussed the unique aspects and challenges of Malibu and
stated the City needed to educate other agencies on those challenges.

Lawrence Myers deferred time to Erik Ran.

Erik Ran discussed his work with MAF. He thanked the Council and the Parks and
Recreation Ad Hoc Committee for their work on the swim programs issue and the
RFQ. He announced that Malibu Marlin swim sign-ups were open.

Robert Shore declined the opportunity to speak.

Patty Mehring discussed her participation in the Masters Swim program.  She
indicated support for the selection of the Malibu Marlin swim program.

Walter Mehring indicated support for Ms. Mehring’s comments and discussed his
family’s participation in local sports programs. He indicated support for Erik Ran’s
coaching.

Benjamin stated Jo Drummond did not live on the City and could not serve as a
Public Works Commissioner. He discussed his research into Ms. Drummond’s
residency.

Bill Sampson expressed opposition to permitting businesses that sold alcohol. He
stated information about Sam Kaplan’s mortgage had been shared by Mayor
   Stewart in his emails.

  Billings Goodenow discussed John Mazza’s behavior as the Planning Commission
  Chair. He discussed Mr. Mazza’s comments during a Planning Commission recess
  in February.

  Mitch Gold discussed his work as the Senior Advisor ofthe Western Zone for USA
  Swimming. He discussed the training philosophies of USA Swimming and the
  focus on long-term development of athletes.

  Jo Drummond stated she did live in the City and was registered to vote in the City.
  She stated she would provide additional documentation to staff.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Lloyd Ahern, Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy Advisory Committee Malibu
  Representative, played a clip reporting on the turnstile at Via Escondido and Mr.
  Ahern’s letter and comments to the Mountains Recreation and Conservation
  Authority (MRCA).

  City Manager McClary discussed SB 1297 and SB 1509 and stated both bills would
  go to the floor of the Assembly this week. He announced Community Lands
  Outreach Phase 2 had launched with in-person events. He stated the land use
  categories in the Community Lands survey were in alphabetical order. He stated
  the outreach included all stakeholders, but 94% of participants in Phase 1 were
  Malibu residents. He stated Environmental Sustainability Department staff was
  creating list of cOmpanies interested in providing Exterior Elevated Element
  inspections to the public. He stated the Temporary Use Pennit Ordinance was
  scheduled for the September 9, 2024 Council meeting. He stated the Housing
  Element had been approved by the Planning Commission and was scheduled for
  the September 23, 2024 Council meeting. He stated the Code of Conduct item was
  scheduled for the October l4, 2024 Council meeting. He announced that City Hall
  would be closed for Labor Day. He announced the City had received an additional
  $1.5 million in Measure M funds for Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) projects. He
  stated he attended a meeting with Captain Seetoo, Mayor Stewart, and
  Councilmember Silverstein to discuss Supreme Court’s decision on Grants Pass v.
  Johnson. He reported on an encampment cleanup on Civic Center this week. He
  stated City staff met with Supervisor Horvath’s staff to discuss the City’s
  environmental programs and the County’s environmental program plans. He
  apologized for delays to ZORACES item regarding code enforcement fines and
  stated it would be scheduled soon. He stated he attended a Malibu Public Facilities
  Authority meeting and the next annual meeting would be in September 2025.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, discussed an
  incident where an individual resisted arrest and barricaded themselves in a vehicle
  on PCH on August 21, 2024. He discussed an incident with a driver with what
  appeared to be a rifle on the Pepperdine University campus. He discussed the
   Stoker family hosting a barbeque for the Beach Team members. He stated Beach
  Team would be operating over Labor Day weekend and extra Deputies would be at
  the Chili Cook—Off.

  The Council thanked Sergeant Soderlund.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Silverstein addressed Ms. Davis and stated he and Councilmember
  Uhring had proposed an Ad Hoc Committee to review the code enforcement fines,
  but it was voted down. He stated Ad Hoc Committees did not require public
  meetings, but members ofthe public could talk to the members. He stated the Code
  of Conduct had been finalized with the City Council Policy Review Ad Hoc
  Committee. He discussed last Planning Commission meeting and thanked
  Commissioner Hill for his service. He requested Interim City Attorney Rusin have
  a conversation with Jo Drummond to confirm her residency. He discussed false
  accusations made during public comment at meetings and the anonymous speakers
  on Zoom.

  Councilmember Grisanti discussed the last Planning Commission meeting.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed speakers on Zoom who may not be residents. He
  stated he did not serve on the Malibu Township Council with Jo Drummond. He
  requested a summary explaining how Planning staff report recommendations were
  being written. He requested staff bring back an item on recommendations for the
  fund balance reserve. He discussed the Community Lands Outreach survey and
  requested clarification on how the survey identified residents.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Deputy City Manager Brown stated the
  Phase One survey results had a filter to break down results by stakeholder groups.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed the Administrative Citation issued to Nobu. He
  stated he leamed about the citation from a reporter and requested the
  Councilmembers be updated before news is shared with the press.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins discussed the last Planning Commission meeting. She
  stated she attended the Parks and Recreation Commission meeting and commended
  the Commissioners for their work on issues related to the swim program. She
  encouraged the public to participate in the Community Lands Outreach Phase 2
  events. She stated she attended a demonstration for fire prevention using goats at
  the Bravo 69 heliport. She indicated support for using goats for brush clearance in
  the City. She stated the ZORACES code enforcement item should be scheduled as
  soon as possible.

  In response to Councilmember Grisanti, Mr. Ahern discussed MRCA’s extensive
  Public Works program and expressed concern regarding the scope of the project.
   Mayor Stewart stated he attended a Malibu Public Facilities Authority meeting and
  an Administrative and Finance Subcommittee meeting on the fee study. He stated
  he attended the Special City Council meeting on good governance and operations.
  He stated he attended a meeting with Councilmember Silverstein to discuss
  overnight camping and enforcement options. He stated the Code of Conduct would
  be brought back soon. He commended the Stoker family for hosting the barbeque.
  He stated ZORACES was the correct body to consider the code enforcement fines.
  He stated staff was working on a fund reserve item and discussed the challenges of
  determining the best reserve minimum. He encouraged the public to participate
  in the Community Lands outreach. He discussed the email chain referenced by Mr.
  Sampson.

  ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a
  motion to approve the Consent Calendar. The motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items

  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full

  2.  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  73200-73379 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 752 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $4,614,568.25. City of Malibu payroll check number 5481-5482 and

  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the June 24, 2024 Regular
  Meeting.
  4.  2023 Multi-Jurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Plan
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-42 adopting the Las
  Virgenes—Malibu Council of Governments 2023 Multi-Jurisdictional
  Hazard Mitigation Plan
  5.  Amendment to Professional Services Agreement for the Pacific Coast
  Highway Right Tum Lane at Trancas Canyon Road
   Racommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1

  Highway Right Tum Lane at Trancas Canyon Road in the amount of
  $34,500, for a total not to exceed $190,440.62.
  6.  Acceptance of Pacific Coast Highway Median Improvements Project
  Recommended Action: 1) Accept the work performed by Stacy and
  Witbeck, Inc. for the Pacific Coast Highway Median Improvements Project,
  Specification No. 2049 as complete; and 2) Authorize the Public Works
  Director to submit for recordation a Notice of Completion.
  7.  Acceptance of Malibu Park Resurfacing Proj ect
  Recommended Action: 1) Accept the work performed by J & H

  10.  Investment Report for the Month Ending July 3 1 , 2024
  Recommended Action: Receive the Investment Report for the month
  ending July 3 l, 2024.
  11.  Dis osal of Su lus Pro e — Wide Format Printer
  Recommended Action: Approve the disposal of surplus City equipment.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS

  White Heart Foundation Fee Waiver
  Recommended Action: Consider whether to approve the request from the White
  Heart Foundation to waive the facility rental fees for the 2024 Ride to the Flags
  event.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the table for discussion.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a
  motion to approve the request from the White Heart Foundation to waive the facility
  rental fees for the 2024 Ride to the Flags event.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to Ryan Sawtelle.

  The motion carried unanimously.
   ITEM 7  COUNCIL ITEMS

  Designation of Voting Delegate and Alternate Voting Delegate(s) for the 2024
  League of California Cities Annual Conference
  Recommended Action: Designate the City’s voting delegate and alternate voting
  delegate(s) for the League of California Cities 2024 Annual Conference scheduled
  for October 16-1 8 in Long Beach.

  City Manager McClary presented the staff report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item.

  MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a
  motion to designate Mayor Pro Tem Riggins as the voting delegate and Mayor
  Stewart as the alternate voting delegate for the League of California Cities 2024
  Annual Conference. The motion carried unanimously.
JAA4  RECESS  At 8:12 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:20
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

  ITEM 4  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  Appeal of Planning Commission Resolution No. 24—009 regarding Coastal
  Development Permit No. 20—0681 Site Plan Review No. 21-009, and Demolition
  Permit No. 20-028 — An application to demolish an existing single-family residence
  and construct a new single-family residence: second unit and associated
  development (6734 Zumirez Drive; Owner/Appellant: IBN Properties, LLC)
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24—44 determining the project is
  categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and
  approving Appeal No. 24-001 , approving Coastal Development Permit (CDP) No.
  20-068 and Demolition Permit (DP) No. 20-028 for the demolition of an existing
  single-family residence and construction of a new 5,860 square foot single—family
  residence, 986 square foot basement, 510 square foot attached garage, 462 square
  foot detached garage, 471 square foot detached second unit, swimming pool, two
  spas, onsite wastewater treatment system (OWTS) and associated development;
  including Site Plan Review (SPR) N0. 21-009 for construction up to 24 feet in
  height for a flat roof, located in the Rural Residential, One-Acre (RR-1) zoning
  district at 6734 Zumirez Drive (IBN Properties, LLC).

  Senior Planner Eaton presented the staff report.

  Disclosures:  Councilmember  Silverstein,  Councilmember  Grisanti,
  Councilmember Uhring, Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, and Mayor Stewart
   The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Stewart opened the fioor to public comment.

  Speakers: Don Schmitz, Mark Johnsson (Casandra Ross, Janet Friesen, and Pat
  Healy deferred time to Mark Johnsson), Ginctta Giovinco, Sose Tezyan, Charlotte
  Jones, Jo Drummond, and Tony Bomkamp

  Don Schmitz provided rebuttal.

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart closed the public hearing
  and returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff and Mr. Schmitz.

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved to adopt Resolution No. 24-44 determining the
  project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), and approving Appeal N0. 24-001, approving Coastal Development
  Permit (CDP) No. 20-068 and Demolition Permit (DP) N0. 20-028 for the
  demolition of an existing single-family residence and construction of a new 5,860
  square foot single—family residence, 986 square foot basement, 510 square foot
  attached garage, 462 square foot detached garage, 471 square foot detached second
  unit, swimming pool, two spas, onsite wastewater treatment system (OWTS) and
  associated development; including Site Plan Review (SPR) No. 21—009 for
  construction up to 24 feet in height for a flat roof, located in the Rural Residential,
  One-Acre (RR-l) zoning district at 6734 Zumirez Drive (IBN Properties, LLC).

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Stewart seconded the motion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  The question was called, and the motion carried 3—2, Councilmember Silverstein
  and Councilmember Uhring opposed.

ITEM 5  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS (Continued)

  Consideration ofNobu Restaurant Conditional Use Permit
  Recommended Action: Receive a preliminary report on Conditional Use Permit
  (CUP) N0. 06—009 and Joint Use Parking Agreement (JUPA) No. 06-001 for
  restaurant and parking operations associated with the Nobu restaurant located at
   22706 Paciflc Coast Highway (PCH) and provide direction as follows: 1) Direct
  Staffto bring forward an item for the Planning Commission to consider whether to
  set a hearing to consider the question ofmodiflcation ofthe CUP to address alleged
  nuisance concerns; 2) Direct Staff to bring forward an item for the Planning
  Commission to consider whether to set a hearing to consider the question of
  revocation of the CUP due to alleged violations of CUP conditions; or 3) Receive
  and flle the report and request Nobu finalize an application for a CUP amendment
  and staff to process the amendment in a timely manner.

  Contract Planner Smith presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: John Jerabek, Jo Drummond, Benjamin Reznik (Gregorio Stephenson
  deferred time to Benjamin Reznik), and Ryan Embree

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff and Mr. Reznik.

  question of modification of the CUP to address alleged nuisance concerns; and 2)

  finalize an application for a CUP amendment direct staffto process the amendment

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins’ motion dies on the floor due to lack of a second.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion
  to direct staff to bring forward an item for the Planning Commission to consider
  whether to set a hearing to consider modifying the Nobu Restaurant CUP, revoking
  the CUP, or amending the CUP, if an application has been finalized by the time of
  the hearing.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff and Mr. Reznik.
   The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.
